stem: To prevent permanent amblyopia, what is the critical timeframe for performing surgery on a child with a unilateral congenital cataract?

options.text: The first $1$ to $4$ weeks of life.
Within the first $6$ months of life.
Only after the child can cooperate with a vision chart.

explanation: Unilateral cataracts are highly amblyogenic, requiring very early intervention to allow for proper visual development.
rationale: Unilateral cases require much faster intervention than bilateral cases to avoid 'lazy eye'.

optionExplanations.A: Unilateral cataracts are highly amblyogenic, requiring very early intervention to allow for proper visual development.
optionExplanations.B: Waiting half a year would result in irreversible amblyopia for a unilateral case.
optionExplanations.C: By this age, the critical period for early visual development in a unilateral case has already passed.
optionExplanations.D: Waiting for behavioral cooperation would delay surgery far beyond the window for effective visual rehabilitation.

source.hint: Unilateral cases require much faster intervention than bilateral cases to avoid 'lazy eye'.
